delete.description:
Cancel a running analysis job (tenant-scoped, race-safe).

The DB cancel is gated on tenant_id and is atomic against concurrent
completion: a wrong-tenant call returns 404, and a job that completes
between the read and the write keeps its terminal status (no lost
update). The in-memory ``cancellation_tokens`` flag and write-through
cache are only updated when the DB cancel actually succeeded.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 if job not found or belongs to another tenant;
        409 if already in a terminal state.

get.description:
Stream scan progress via Server-Sent Events (feature-flagged).

Deliberately NOT ``Depends(get_db)``. FastAPI closes a yield-dependency only
after the response completes, and this response completes when the job
reaches a terminal status -- which can be many minutes, or never if the
client just leaves the tab open. A ``SessionDep`` here therefore pins one
pgbouncer server connection ``idle in transaction`` (the RLS binding opens a
``SET LOCAL`` transaction) for the whole stream.

The stream body reads progress from Redis and touches no table at all, so
the only database work is the ownership pre-flight below -- which takes a
short-lived session and gives it straight back.

501.description: SSE progress feature is not enabled

get.description:
Compare findings between two critique jobs.

Supports before/after deltas across mixed input modes (e.g. a live-URL
"before" vs a static html/artifact "after"). ``compute_score_deltas``
treats a category present on only one side as ``0.0`` on the other, so the
call never errors — but the result is **semantically asymmetric**: a static
job runs a strict subset of checks (seo base only, security HTML-subset
only; no seo_live / live-security / adapters), so ``seo``/``security``
deltas are not apples-to-apples and categories present on one side only
yield full-value deltas. Each job's ``progress.input_mode`` /
``progress.skipped_categories`` disclose which side was static.

post.description:
Batch extract brands from multiple URLs concurrently.

Concurrency is bounded by the process-wide browser gate in
``src/shared/security/browser_gate.py``, which every pipeline run passes
through at the fetch stage -- so the 50-URL ceiling on the request body is
not itself a ceiling on resident browsers, and does not need to be.

Upstream 402 — why this endpoint does NOT re-emit it, unlike its siblings
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
``/brand/from-url`` and ``/brands/compare`` answer the caller with the
upstream 402, because a single-result endpoint has nothing to return without
it. This one does: ``byo_llm_not_configured`` costs a brand its tagline,
voice and industry, and NOTHING else — colors, fonts, logo and palette come
from the page, not from the LLM. Failing the whole request would throw away
50 completed Playwright fetches over a condition that removes a handful of
fields, and the endpoint's documented contract is already per-URL partial
success.

So the LLM-less work is kept: the first URL to hit the 402 retries itself
with the ``llm_analysis`` stage disabled, and every URL that has not yet
built its context skips the stage from the start rather than paying another
doomed WM call. Each such result carries ``llm_analysis`` in its
``extraction_report.stages_failed`` — honest per-URL, and enough for
:func:`_is_cacheable` to keep it out of Redis without a second rule.

The tenant-level fact is reported ONCE, structured, in
``upstream_error``: 50 copies of ``str(exc)`` in ``errors`` told the SPA
nothing it could branch on and leaked the internal WM URL while doing it.

Download and store a logo from a URL.

The tenant is taken from the authenticated identity on the request and is
never client-supplied. The blob is written to storage under that tenant's
prefix before the asset row is inserted, so a body-settable tenant would let
a caller plant bytes in another tenant's prefix even though RLS then
refused the row — the DB check is not the only thing guarding this path.

post.description:
Compare brand identities between two domains.

Args:
    body: Request with two domains and optional extract_if_missing flag.
    request: FastAPI request with tenant context.
    db: Async database session.

Returns:
    Comparison result with similarity score and field-level comparisons.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 if either brand not found; 402 when an on-demand
        extraction hit a caller-fixable upstream condition (see below).

Why a passthrough 402 fails the WHOLE compare rather than being reported
per-brand: it is not a fact about ``domain_a``, it is a fact about the
TENANT — ``byo_llm_not_configured`` means *no* extraction in this request,
or any other, can run the LLM stage, so a per-brand error channel would say
the same sentence twice and still leave us unable to build the comparison.
And there is nowhere to say it: ``BrandComparisonResponse`` requires two
fully-populated brands and has no per-brand error field, so the only
alternatives are the 402 or a **404 "Brand not found"** — which is a lie
that sends the tenant looking for a missing brand instead of to Settings.
A batch endpoint, whose contract IS per-URL partial success, resolves the
same trade-off the other way (see ``routes.batch_extract``).

402.description: Tenant action required upstream (e.g. LLM provider not configured)

post.description:
Fetch a URL and return a flat, grounded GTM/ICP record.

Fail-closed: any fetch/LLM/shape failure raises ``502`` — a fabricated
``200`` is never returned. Ungrounded keys are omitted (recon reads them as
``unknown``).

The one exception to "everything is a 502" is a genuinely caller-fixable
upstream status (today only ``402``, e.g. the tenant has not configured an
LLM provider), which is re-emitted with the upstream's actionable
``{code, message}`` — see :mod:`src.shared.upstream_errors`. It is still
fail-closed: no fabricated ``200``, just an honest status.

AuthInfo.title: AuthInfo
AuthInfo.description:
Authentication info the orchestrator forwards on behalf of the
end-user so analysis_service can access an authenticated target site.

Three modes are supported in this MVP:

  - ``type="none"`` (default)   no auth applied
  - ``type="basic"``            HTTP Basic with username + password
  - ``type="bearer"``           Authorization: Bearer <token>
  - ``type="cookies"``          replay a pre-collected cookie jar

Notes / non-goals for this MVP:

  - Form-login (POST username/password to login_url, persist session
    cookies for subsequent requests) is intentionally NOT implemented
    here. Callers wanting form-login should perform the login
    themselves and pass the resulting session cookies via
    ``type="cookies"``.
  - MFA / OAuth / SAML flows are out of scope.
  - This schema is consumed today by ``_fetch_html`` in
    ``services/critique_service/helpers.py``. Per-scanner threading
    (security_scanner, network_checks, code_quality_scanner, axe-core
    Playwright context, ...) is tracked as a follow-up — they each
    spin their own ``httpx.AsyncClient`` and will see unauthenticated
    traffic until they're updated. For sites that gate ONLY the page
    HTML (the common case), the MVP is enough.

BatchUpstreamError.title: BatchUpstreamError
BatchUpstreamError.description:
A batch-wide upstream condition the CALLER has to fix.

Distinct from ``BatchExtractResponse.errors`` on purpose. ``errors`` is
per-URL and opaque (a string); this is the ONE tenant-level fact that
applies to every URL in the batch — today ``byo_llm_not_configured`` from
``worker_management``. Repeating it 50 times as 50 opaque strings told the
SPA nothing it could branch on, and the batch still answered 200. Carrying
the same ``code`` the ``/api/brand/from-url`` 402 envelope carries lets one
frontend branch render the same "Open Settings" call-to-action.

artifact_ref.title: Artifact Ref
artifact_ref.description: Relative object key to read S2S and score in lieu of a URL, resolved strictly inside the calling tenant's own prefix. The bucket is fixed server-side and is analysis_service's own bucket, NOT html_render_service's — so refs naming a rendered artifact currently return 'not found' (see CritiqueRequest docstring). The key is used literally: percent-encoded refs, URI forms (minio://, s3://, file://, http://) and any key escaping the tenant prefix are rejected with 400.

CritiqueRequest.title: CritiqueRequest
CritiqueRequest.description:
Request to start a website critique.

Exactly one content source is required — one of ``url``, ``html``, or
``artifact_ref``:

  - ``url``           crawl a live, reachable page (the historical path;
                      runs every category incl. live-only checks).
  - ``html``          score a pre-rendered HTML string in place (no fetch).
  - ``artifact_ref``  read a stored object out of **analysis_service's own
                      MinIO bucket** (S2S) and score it in place. The key is
                      confined server-side to the calling tenant's prefix —
                      see ``CritiqueHelpersMixin._artifact_object_key``.

                      ⚠️ This source is **not usable today**: the read
                      resolves against this service's own bucket (whose only
                      writer is the brand-logo upload), NOT against
                      html_render_service's store, so a ref naming a
                      rendered artifact returns "not found". Use ``html``
                      instead until the follow-up described on
                      ``CritiqueHelpersMixin.ARTIFACT_BUCKET`` lands.

For ``html``/``artifact_ref`` (no live origin) the live-only work is skipped
— ``seo_live`` (robots/sitemap/llms.txt), the live-security checks
(headers/TLS/CORS/exposed-files), and the external adapters (axe/lighthouse).
The static scanners (seo base, accessibility, performance, ux, cro, and the
HTML-only security subset) run as usual. Which categories were scored vs
skipped is surfaced in the job's ``progress`` (``input_mode``,
``scored_categories``, ``skipped_categories``) — never silently.

LogoDownloadRequest.title: LogoDownloadRequest
LogoDownloadRequest.description:
Request to download and store a logo.

Carries no tenant field. It used to have one (``tenant_id``, a body-supplied
"override"), and that made the request the authority on which tenant's blob
prefix got written: ``LogoService.download_and_store`` calls
``storage.store(tenant_id, ...)`` *before* the route inserts the asset row,
so RLS's ``WITH CHECK`` refused the row while the image had already landed
in the victim tenant's object storage. The tenant now comes only from the
authenticated identity on the request.

``extra="forbid"`` is the other half of that removal. Pydantic's default is
``extra="ignore"``, which means a client still sending the old ``tenant_id``
gets a **200 against a different tenant than it asked for** and no
indication that the field it supplied was dropped. Silently doing the right
thing while the caller believes it asked for something else is the worst of
the available behaviours for a field that was removed on tenant-isolation
grounds: it is indistinguishable, from the caller's side, from the
vulnerable version still working. A 422 naming the unexpected key says
exactly what changed.

Verified safe before enabling: no service in the monorepo POSTs to
``/api/brand/logo/download`` at all. The orchestrator's
``brand_extractor_client`` posts ``{"url", "download_logo"}`` to the
*different* ``/api/brand/from-url`` route, which is unaffected.

include_grounding.description: Opt in to the WM claim-grounding pass (A18): fact-check each written recommendation against the page text; unsupported advice is dropped (SOFT gate). Meaningful only with include_recommendations. Off by default (byte-identical); fail-soft.

include_exec_summary.title: Include Exec Summary
include_exec_summary.description: Opt in to the WM exec-summary worker (A2): a short grounded narrative plus an id-locked fix roadmap over the computed scores. Meaningful only with include_llm. Off by default (byte-identical); fail-soft.

include_critic.title: Include Critic
include_critic.description: Opt in to the WM report-critic (A11): a holistic ship gate that re-writes only the recommendations it flags as generic/ungrounded. Meaningful only with include_recommendations. Off by default (byte-identical); fail-soft.

intent.title: Intent
intent.description: Optional page intent (audience / goal) used only to steer the opt-in recommendation-writer prose (include_llm). Ignored on the deterministic path.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: Optional supporting source texts to ground recommendations against, in addition to the scanned page (used only with include_grounding). Each string is a source excerpt; capped/clipped downstream.

competitor_urls.title: Competitor Urls
competitor_urls.description: Optional competitor page URLs for the opt-in content-gap analyzer. Runs only when include_llm=true. Capped at 3.

cross_page_linking.title: Cross Page Linking
cross_page_linking.description: Opt in to cross-page internal-linking analysis (sitemap crawl for orphan / broken-link / hub signals). Network + page-capped; off by default so the fast deterministic sync contract is unchanged.

max_pages.title: Max Pages
max_pages.description: Page cap for the cross-page internal-linking crawl (max 50).

SeoAuditRequest.title: SeoAuditRequest
SeoAuditRequest.description:
SEO audit request — exactly one of ``url`` or ``html`` is required.

Adds the opt-in competitor content-gap + cross-page crawl fields on top of the
shared ``url``/``html``/``include_llm`` scorecard base.

group_scores.title: Group Scores
group_scores.description: Per-group 0-100 score; null for a group that was not measured

source.title: Source

llm_enriched.description: Whether Tier-3 LLM judgments were applied

unmeasured_groups.title: Unmeasured Groups
unmeasured_groups.description: Groups whose scanner did not run (e.g. the cross-page linking crawl timed out). Always includes `performance`, which this path never measures (weight 0, outside the rubric). These groups are excluded from overall_score rather than being credited a perfect 100.

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: Share of the total group weight that was actually measured (0-1). 1.0 means overall_score covers the full rubric.

projection.description: Score lift from fixing top findings (only when include_projection)

exec_summary.description: Executive summary + id-locked roadmap (only when include_exec_summary)
